curriculum.lesson_evidence: Relaxation helps the body and mind slow down. Mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment on purpose, such as noticing your breathing, sounds or how your body feels. Simple activities include a body scan (relaxing one part at a time), mindful listening (hearing as many sounds as you can) and mindful walking. These can help us feel calm and focused. If an activity feels uncomfortable, you can stop or open your eyes.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write the steps of a one-minute mindful listening activity and when it could help.

FEEDBACK
Steps: sit quietly, close or soften your eyes, listen for sounds near and far for one minute, then name them. It can help before a test or after a busy playtime.

WATCH FOR
Thinking mindfulness means emptying your mind. It means noticing what is happening and gently bringing attention back.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Do three relaxation or mindfulness activities (a body scan, mindful listening, five senses stop) over the week. Record your calm rating before and after each and which you prefer. Teach one to a family member.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
